label: D2 after a common a2->S2 transition, previous trial rewarded and a2 repeated (mid-episode)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (never at D1 or GO), and essentially only when the agent chose a2 and reached S2 via the common transition (in_action == 2 & in_state == 2; 12 of 58690 active steps are not). Within that, it needs the previous trial to have been rewarded (prev_reward == 0 holds 0.1% of the mass) and the previous choice not to have been a1, so it is a rewarded-stay-on-a2 / S2-is-good signal. It also has a strong episode-clock dependence: silent on episode trials 0-9 and 90-99, highest around trials 50-70, which the GRU must track internally. All predicate variables are observed by D2. Dev: P 0.74, R 0.98, F1 0.84, mass recall 1.00; the base conjunction without the clock and prev_action terms gets F1 0.75. From the example windows, magnitude seems to grow over runs of consecutive rewarded a2->S2 common trials, and it co-occurs with high value (24.7% firing rate in the top value bin vs about 2% in the middle bins). I did not quantify the magnitude effect. Never fires on a1, S1, rare transitions, or reward-input steps. The remaining false positives are qualifying D2 steps where it stays silent, usually early in a streak.

issues: The factual claims hold on dev. The unit fires only at D2 (D1 and GO have 0 active steps). 58678 of 58690 active steps have in_action==2 and 58687 have in_state==2. Only 9 active steps follow a rare transition. prev_reward==0 carries 0.1% of the activation mass. Trials 0-9 have 214 active steps (0.3%), trials 90-99 have none, and the peak is at trials 50-70. Reported test scores reproduce: P 0.710, R 0.980, F1 0.824.

The clock is a soft ramp, not a 10-90 window. Precision of the predicate climbs steadily: 0.34 at ep_trial 10-11, 0.49 at 12-13, 0.62 at 18-19, 0.78 at 26-27, 0.85-0.89 at 50-71. It then falls off sharply: 0.67 at 82-83, 0.42 at 84-85, 0.10 at 86-87, 0.006 at 88-89. Narrowing the window to ep_trial 13-85 alone raises test F1 from 0.824 to 0.849, so the hard cutoff at 90 includes about 4000 dead steps.

The condition is an a2 choice streak, not just the previous choice. If trial t-2 was a1 (with t-1 a2 and rewarded), precision is 0.024 (n=1069). If t-3 was a1, precision is 0.37. The label only conditions on the previous choice.

Reward history beyond one trial matters. With an a2 choice at t-2, precision is 0.87 if the t-2 reward was 1 and 0.58 if it was 0. If both t-2 and t-3 were unrewarded, precision is 0.42. This is a systematic false-positive class, which partly matches the stated 'early in a streak'.

The 'S2-is-good signal' reading overclaims. When the previous trial was a2 to S1 (rare) and rewarded, which is evidence that S1 is good, the predicate still has precision 0.55. With good==1 it has precision 0.41. Conversely, a previous a1 to S2 rare rewarded trial (evidence that S2 is good) gives precision 0.001. So the unit tracks a rewarded a2 choice streak, not model-based belief that S2 is good.

prev_action != 1 mostly serves to admit rel -3 steps, where prev_action is -1 (unknown in the window). That accounts for 24% of the mass; prev_action==2 alone gives recall 0.75. This is a window artifact, not a flaw, but it should be stated.
The magnitude claim (activation grows over runs of rewarded common a2 to S2 trials) was not measured. It is consistent with the history effects above.
skeptic.revised_label: D2 after a common a2->S2 transition, during a rewarded streak of a2 choices (no a1 in the last 2-3 trials); gated by a soft episode-clock ramp that rises from about trial 12, peaks at 50-70 and is gone by about trial 87
